title: Finite-Horizon Fisher Memory in Two-Sided Power-Bounded Recurrent Systems
abstract: arXiv:2609.39800v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We analyse allocation, admission and post-write retention in finite-horizon linear-Gaussian noisy recurrent memories. At every horizon, the directional Fisher memory $M_n$ satisfies $\operatorname{tr}M_n=N$: non-normality redistributes information but cannot raise its spherical average, while normal carriers satisfy $M_n=I$. For bi-power-bounded carriers, we derive uniform $1/n$ lag bounds, identify the limit of $M_n$ with the inverse of the classical Ces\`aro asymptotic limit of $W^\top$, and give finite-horizon error bounds. A time-varying coupling defines an end-to-end store operator. The writer-optimal direction need not be store-optimal. After writing ends, an invertible hold preserves the full stored Fisher matrix. Additive contamination bounded by $\alpha$ times the closure covariance retains at least $1/(1+\alpha)$ of that matrix; a covariance-aware decoder attains the corresponding accuracy. translated_title: 双侧幂有界递归系统中的有限时域Fisher记忆
translated_abstract: 我们分析了有限时域线性高斯噪声递归记忆中的信息分配、准入与写入后保持问题。在每个时域长度下，方向性Fisher记忆 $M_n$ 满足 $\operatorname{tr}M_n=N$：非正规性只会重新分配信息，但无法提升其球面平均值，而正规载体会满足 $M_n=I$。对于双侧幂有界的载体，我们推导出一致的 $1/n$ 滞后界，将 $M_n$ 的极限等同于 $W^\top$ 的经典Cesàro渐近极限的逆，并给出有限时域误差界。时变耦合定义了一个端到端的存储算子。写入最优的方向未必是存储最优的方向。写入结束后，可逆的保持操作能够完整保留已存储的Fisher矩阵；受 $\alpha$ 倍闭包协方差约束的加性污染可使该矩阵至少保留 $1/(1+\alpha)$，而协方差感知的解码器能够达到相应的精度。在递归载体固定的情况下……
tldr: 该论文证明了在有限时域噪声递归记忆中方向性Fisher信息的迹恒为载体维度（非正规性只重新分配信息），并为双侧幂有界系统导出一致的1/n滞后界、刻画了写入最优与存储最优方向的差异，以及污染下至少保持1/(1+α)存储Fisher矩阵的鲁棒性界。
en_tdlr: The paper proves that in finite-horizon linear-Gaussian noisy recurrent memories the directional Fisher memory has trace N (non-normality only redistributes information), derives uniform 1/n lag bounds and Cesàro-limit characterizations for bi-power-bounded carriers, shows the writer-optimal direction need not be store-optimal, and establishes that α-bounded additive contamination retains at least 1/(1+α) of the stored Fisher matrix.
